options.A: To collect insurance and payment details from victims
options.B: To sort and prioritize patients based on injury severity
options.C: To discharge healthy staff members so they can go home
options.D: To clean and disinfect the emergency room floors

explanation: Triage allows medical personnel to quickly identify and treat those with life-threatening injuries first when resources are limited. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T7#GNS112_U4_T7_h7)

question: Why are early symptoms like mild memory slips and tiredness often tricky to diagnose right away?

options.A: They always appear alongside total paralysis
options.B: They disappear completely within twenty-four hours
options.C: They only occur during strenuous physical exercise
options.D: They easily mimic normal aging and everyday tiredness

explanation: It's easy to miss the early clues because they look just like everyday stress, fatigue, or getting older!

question: Why is checking the bladder so important in the first few hours after childbirth?

options.A: Urinary retention always leads to permanent kidney failure
options.B: A full bladder pushes the uterus out of place and causes heavy bleeding
options.C: Bladder fullness is the primary sign of postpartum preeclampsia
options.D: It prevents the lochia from changing from red to white

explanation: Think of it this way: a full bladder takes up space and pushes against the uterus, stopping it from contracting properly. Keeping the bladder empty keeps mom safe from extra bleeding!

question: An older adult with low vision is going home from the clinic. What is the most important home safety tip to give them?

options.A: Keep all windows covered to block glaring sunlight
options.B: Paint all interior walls a bright, shiny white
options.C: Improve indoor lighting and clear away tripping hazards like loose rugs
options.D: Install tinted glass windows throughout the house

explanation: Good lighting helps them make the absolute most of their remaining sight, and clearing out clutter keeps them safe from nasty falls.

question: Which patient has the highest risk of developing cholesterol gallstones?

options.A: An elderly male who exercises daily and eats low-fat meals
options.B: An adolescent male eating a high-protein diet
options.C: A young adult female with a low body mass index
options.D: A middle-aged female who lost weight very rapidly

explanation: Great thinking! Being female, middle-aged, and undergoing rapid weight loss are classic risk factors due to hormonal shifts and bile changes.

question: What factor most determines what kind of birth defect a teratogen will cause?

options.A: Whether the placenta is anterior or posterior
options.B: Total volume of amniotic fluid present
options.C: Gestational age at the time of exposure
options.D: The mother's blood type and Rhesus factor

explanation: Brilliant! Timing is everything because different organs develop at different weeks; exposure during organogenesis causes structural issues, while later exposure affects growth. You nailed it!

question: What is the true purpose of doing an Apgar score in the delivery room?

options.A: To diagnose long-term brain disabilities
options.B: To see how well the baby is adjusting to life outside
options.C: To decide the exact second resuscitation must start
options.D: To predict future intelligence in school

explanation: Resuscitation actually starts before the 1-minute Apgar is even done! The score just helps us see how the baby is responding and adapting over those first few minutes.

question: What term is used to describe a dangerously low fasting blood sugar level?

options.A: Hypoglycemia
options.B: Hemoconcentration
options.C: Glycosuria
options.D: Hyperglycemia

explanation: Hypoglycemia refers to blood glucose levels falling below the normal healthy threshold, typically under 70 mg/dL. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T12#GNS221_U2_T12_h7)

question: An Alzheimer's patient gets very confused every late afternoon. Which nursing action helps best?

options.A: Restrict all fluid intake after noon to prevent bathroom trips
options.B: Establish a calm, predictable daily routine with engaging daytime activities
options.C: Change the patient's daily care schedule constantly to keep them alert
options.D: Keep the room dark and quiet all day to encourage deep rest

explanation: Spot on! Predictable routines and daytime activities help prevent 'sundowning' (late-day confusion) by keeping them secure and engaged. Great care planning!

question: What happens during the 'tonic' phase of a seizure?

options.A: Rapid wandering around the room
options.B: Sudden return of normal alertness
options.C: Sudden stiffening of the body muscles
options.D: Total relaxation and limpness of limbs

explanation: You got it! Think of 'tonic' as 'tone' or stiffness—the body goes rigid abruptly.

question: What gland releases follicle-stimulating hormone and luteinizing hormone?

options.A: Posterior pituitary gland
options.B: Hypothalamus
options.C: Anterior pituitary gland
options.D: Adrenal cortex

explanation: The anterior pituitary gland responds to signals from the hypothalamus by secreting follicle-stimulating hormone and luteinizing hormone into the bloodstream. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T12#GNS311_U1_T12_h1)

question: Why do we need a team approach when caring for older adults?

options.A: Families refuse to take care of older relatives at home
options.B: Physicians are no longer legally permitted to work alone
options.C: Older adults usually have multiple overlapping health and social issues
options.D: Hospitals require multidisciplinary teams for financial funding

explanation: Aging bodies often deal with several health challenges at once. Working as a team brings different experts together to handle these complex needs much better than any single person could!

question: What is the primary clinical use of an intradermal injection?

options.A: Rapid pain relief
options.B: Diagnostic testing
options.C: Intravenous hydration
options.D: Immediate blood pressure support

explanation: Intradermal injections are used mostly for diagnostic tests like tuberculosis screening and allergy checks because they allow slow absorption in the skin layer. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T6#GNS122_U1_T6_h1)

question: Which sudden problem can happen if the vagus nerve gets accidentally stimulated during traction setup?

options.A: Yellow discoloration of the skin
options.B: Sudden high fever and chills
options.C: Severe drop in heart rate
options.D: Inability to move the toes

explanation: The vagus nerve is powerful! Triggering it can cause the heart rate to slow right down and make the patient feel faint.

question: What does client-centered contraceptive counseling prioritize above all else?

options.A: The personal reproductive goals and choices of the client
options.B: The hospital policy on family planning targets
options.C: The nurse's personal preference for birth control methods
options.D: The fastest and cheapest method available in the clinic

explanation: Client-centered care centers entirely on the individual's needs, preferences, and life circumstances rather than outside pressures. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T015#GNS226_U5_T015_h2)

question: What is a major personal benefit of joining a professional nursing body as a student or young nurse?

options.A: Automatic pay raises negotiated by the national body
options.B: Guaranteed promotion to head nurse within a year
options.C: Opportunities for networking and career growth
options.D: Exemption from paying annual state license renewal fees

explanation: Joining lets you connect with senior nurses and mentors who can help guide your career path and open doors to exciting opportunities!

question: What makes a mouth sore suspicious for oral cancer rather than a normal, everyday canker sore?

options.A: It is extremely painful when eating citrus
options.B: It appears directly on the tip of the tongue
options.C: It goes away and returns every few months
options.D: It fails to heal within two weeks

explanation: As a rule of thumb in nursing, any sore in the mouth that hangs around for more than two weeks needs a closer look and a possible biopsy.
